q: A bottle contains 0.6 liter of sterile saline. A nurse pours out 3 doses of 85 milliliters each for wound care. How many milliliters of saline remain in the bottle? Enter your answer in milliliters.

tr.5745: Converted 0.6 L to 6,000 mL (four places) before subtracting 255 mL.

w: Convert the bottle to milliliters: 0.6 L × 1,000 = 600 mL. Amount poured = 3 × 85 = 255 mL. Remaining = 600 - 255 = 345 mL.

q: A child who weighs 18 kilograms is prescribed a medication at 15 milligrams per kilogram per day, divided into 3 equal doses. How many grams of the medication are in each dose? Enter your answer in grams.

tr.90: Stopped at milligrams; the question asks for grams.
tr.0.27: Gave the full daily amount (270 mg = 0.27 g) instead of one of the 3 doses.

w: Daily amount = 15 mg × 18 = 270 mg. Each dose = 270 ÷ 3 = 90 mg. Milligrams to grams: divide by 1,000, so 90 mg = 0.09 g.

q: A pharmacy technician is sorting five powder samples by mass. The labels use different metric units. Place the samples in order from least mass to greatest mass, starting with the least.
A lab technician has 2.5 liters of a buffer solution. Each test tube must be filled with exactly 15 milliliters of the solution. How many test tubes can be completely filled from the 2.5 liters?
w: 2.5 L × 1,000 = 2,500 mL. 2,500 ÷ 15 = 166.67. Only complete tubes count, so round down to 166.

n.1: This treats 2.5 L as 25,000 mL (multiplying by 10,000); 1 L = 1,000 mL.

q: A wound measured 3.4 centimeters long when it was assessed on Monday. On Friday, the same wound measured 27 millimeters long. By how many millimeters did the length of the wound decrease?
w: 3.4 cm × 10 = 34 mm. Decrease = 34 - 27 = 7 mm.

n.1: This subtracts 3.4 from 27 without first converting 3.4 cm to millimeters.
n.2: 0.7 is the decrease in centimeters; 0.7 cm = 7 mm.
n.3: This converts 3.4 cm to 340 mm by multiplying by 100; 1 cm = 10 mm.

q: A nutrition study records each participant's fluid intake in deciliters. One participant drank 1.8 liters of water during the day. How many deciliters should the researcher record for this participant?
w: Deci- means one tenth, so 1 L = 10 dL. 1.8 × 10 = 18 dL.

n.0: This uses 100 per liter, which is the centiliter factor (1 L = 100 cL).
n.1: This uses 1,000 per liter, which is the milliliter factor (1 L = 1,000 mL).
n.3: This divides by 10. A deciliter is smaller than a liter, so the number of deciliters must be larger.

q: Four specimen containers are labeled with their capacities: container W holds 0.45 L, container X holds 405 mL, container Y holds 4.6 dL, and container Z holds 44 cL. Which container has the greatest capacity?
w: Convert to milliliters: W = 0.45 × 1,000 = 450 mL; X = 405 mL; Y = 4.6 × 100 = 460 mL; Z = 44 × 10 = 440 mL. Container Y holds the most.

n.1: 405 is the largest number shown, but 405 mL is less than 450 mL and 460 mL.
n.2: 44 cL = 440 mL, which is less than 460 mL.
n.3: 0.45 L = 450 mL, which is less than 4.6 dL = 460 mL.

q: An IV infusion pump delivers fluid at a constant rate of 125 milliliters per hour. If the rate is not changed, how many liters of fluid will the patient receive during a 12-hour shift?

n.0: This divides 1,500 mL by 100 instead of 1,000.
n.1: This divides 1,500 mL by 10,000 instead of 1,000.
n.3: This is the amount for one hour (125 mL); multiply by the 12 hours first.

q: A nurse records a newborn's weight as 7 pounds 13 ounces. The nursery's electronic scale displays weight in ounces. What weight, in ounces, should the scale display for this newborn?

n.0: This uses 10 ounces per pound, treating pounds like a decimal unit; 1 lb = 16 oz.
n.1: This uses 12 ounces per pound; 1 lb = 16 oz.
n.3: This converts the 7 pounds (7 × 16 = 112 oz) but does not add the 13 ounces.

q: A roll of medical tape is 5 yards long. A nurse cuts strips that are each 8 inches long to secure dressings. How many complete 8-inch strips can be cut from the roll?
w: 5 yd × 36 in per yd = 180 in. 180 ÷ 8 = 22.5, so 22 complete strips can be cut.

n.0: This uses 12 inches per yard (5 yd = 60 in); 1 yd = 36 in.
n.1: 180 ÷ 8 = 22.5, and half a strip is not a complete strip, so round down.
n.3: This uses 10 inches per foot (15 ft = 150 in); 1 ft = 12 in.

q: For a clinic open house, each of 5 tables needs 3 quarts of lemonade. The lemonade is sold in half-gallon jugs. What is the least number of jugs that must be bought to supply all 5 tables?
w: Total = 5 × 3 = 15 qt. A gallon is 4 qt, so a half gallon is 2 qt. 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5, so round up to 8 jugs.

n.2: This multiplies 15 quarts by 2 instead of dividing by the 2 quarts in each jug.
n.3: 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5, and 7 jugs hold 14 qt, which is not enough, so round up.

q: An IV infusion is started at 9:40 a.m. and is programmed to run for 2.6 hours without stopping. At what time will the infusion finish?

n.0: This reads 2.6 hours as 260 minutes (4 h 20 min).
n.1: This reads 2.6 hours as 2 hours 6 minutes; 0.6 h = 0.6 × 60 = 36 min.
n.2: This reads 0.6 hour as 60 minutes, as if an hour had 100 minutes.

q: A patient's intake record shows 2 cups of water, 1 pint of juice, and 12 fluid ounces of tea during one shift. What was the patient's total intake for the shift? Enter your answer in fluid ounces.

tr.36: Counted the pint as 8 fl oz (one cup); 1 pint = 2 cups = 16 fl oz.
tr.76: Used 16 fl oz per cup and 32 fl oz per pint (the quart value).

q: A school track measures 440 yards per lap. A student training for a fitness test wants to walk exactly 3 miles on the track. How many laps must the student walk? Enter the number of laps.

tr.4: Found the laps in one mile (1,760 ÷ 440) but not in 3 miles.

q: A recipe for a hospital cafeteria lists 3 quarts of vegetable stock. Which of the following amounts are equal to 3 quarts? Select all that apply.
w: 1 qt = 2 pints = 4 cups = 32 fl oz, and 1 gal = 4 qt. So 3 qt = 12 cups = 96 fl oz = 6 pints = 3/4 gal = 0.75 gal.

n.2: 3 qt = 6 pints; 4 pints is 2 quarts.
n.4: This uses 16 fl oz per quart, which is the pint value; 1 qt = 32 fl oz.

q: A delivery van can safely carry a load of no more than 1.5 tons. Each crate of medical supplies weighs 140 pounds. What is the greatest number of crates the van can carry on one trip?

n.0: This reads 1.5 tons as 1 ton 500 pounds (2,500 lb); 0.5 ton = 1,000 lb.
n.2: 3,000 ÷ 140 = 21.4, and 22 crates weigh 3,080 lb, which is over the limit, so round down.
n.3: This uses 1,000 pounds per ton; 1 ton = 2,000 lb.

q: A board is 8 feet 3 inches long. A carpenter cuts off a piece that is 2 feet 7 inches long. Ignoring the width of the saw cut, how long is the remaining piece of board?
w: Borrow 1 foot: 8 ft 3 in = 7 ft 15 in. 7 ft 15 in - 2 ft 7 in = 5 ft 8 in. Check: 99 in - 31 in = 68 in = 5 ft 8 in.

n.1: This borrows 12 inches correctly but does not reduce the 8 feet to 7 feet.
n.2: This borrows 1 foot as 10 inches (13 - 7 = 6); 1 ft = 12 in, so 15 - 7 = 8.
n.3: This subtracts 3 from 7 instead of borrowing a foot from the 8 feet.

q: A patient in a cardiac rehabilitation program walks 1 mile in 16 minutes at a steady pace. What is the patient's walking speed in feet per second?

n.0: 330 is the speed in feet per minute (5,280 ÷ 16); divide by 60 to get feet per second.
n.1: This divides seconds by feet (960 ÷ 5,280), which gives seconds per foot.
n.3: 3.75 is the speed in miles per hour (60 ÷ 16), not feet per second.

q: Brand A oatmeal costs $5.28 for a 1.5-pound canister. Brand B oatmeal costs $4.60 for a 20-ounce canister. Which brand costs less per ounce, and by how much per ounce?
w: 1.5 lb × 16 = 24 oz. Brand A: $5.28 ÷ 24 = $0.22 per oz. Brand B: $4.60 ÷ 20 = $0.23 per oz. Brand A is cheaper by $0.01 per ounce.

n.0: This treats 1.5 lb as 15 oz. Since 1.5 lb = 24 oz, Brand A costs $0.22 per ounce.
n.2: This uses 12 oz per pound (1.5 lb = 18 oz); 1 lb = 16 oz.
n.3: $0.16 is the difference per pound ($3.52 vs. $3.68), not per ounce.

q: A hallway is 42 yards long. Baseboard trim is sold in 8-foot pieces. How many pieces must be bought to run trim along both long sides of the hallway? Assume there are no doorways.
w: 42 yd × 3 = 126 ft per side, so both sides = 252 ft. 252 ÷ 8 = 31.5, so round up to 32 pieces.

n.0: 252 ÷ 8 = 31.5, and 31 pieces fall 4 feet short, so round up.
n.1: This does not convert yards to feet (84 ÷ 8 = 10.5, so 11); 1 yd = 3 ft.
n.2: This covers one side (126 ÷ 8 = 15.75, so 16); trim is needed on both sides.

q: A patient weighed 187 pounds at admission and 176 pounds at discharge. The chart records weight in kilograms. Use 1 kilogram = 2.2 pounds. How many kilograms did the patient lose during the hospital stay?

n.0: This multiplies the 11 lb loss by 2.2; pounds to kilograms means dividing by 2.2.
n.1: 11 is the loss in pounds; it still has to be divided by 2.2.
n.3: 85 kg is the admission weight (187 ÷ 2.2), not the amount lost.

q: A patient's height is measured as 5 feet 4 inches, but the electronic record requires height in centimeters. Use 1 inch = 2.54 centimeters. What height should be entered, to the nearest tenth of a centimeter?
w: 5 ft 4 in = 5 × 12 + 4 = 64 in. 64 × 2.54 = 162.56 cm, which rounds to 162.6 cm.

n.1: This converts the 5 feet (60 in) but leaves out the 4 inches.
n.2: This reads 5 ft 4 in as 54 inches; it is 5 × 12 + 4 = 64 in.
n.3: This divides 64 by 2.54; inches to centimeters means multiplying by 2.54.

q: Jordan finishes a 10-kilometer charity run in 50 minutes. Use 1 mile = 1.6 kilometers. What was Jordan's average speed for the run in miles per hour?

n.0: 12 is the speed in kilometers per hour; convert 10 km to 6.25 mi first.
n.2: This multiplies 10 km by 1.6; kilometers to miles means dividing by 1.6.
n.3: This treats 50 minutes as 0.5 hour; 50 min = 50/60 of an hour.

q: A container of protein powder holds 2 pounds of powder. Each scoop holds 30 grams. Use 1 ounce = 28 grams. How many full scoops of powder does the container hold?
w: 2 lb × 16 = 32 oz. 32 × 28 = 896 g. 896 ÷ 30 = 29.87, so the container holds 29 full scoops.

n.0: This multiplies 2 lb by 2.2 as if converting to kilograms (4.4 kg); pounds to kilograms means dividing.
n.1: This uses 10 ounces per pound (20 oz = 560 g); 1 lb = 16 oz.
n.3: 896 ÷ 30 = 29.9, and the 30th scoop would not be full, so round down.

q: A traveler rents a car in Canada, where gasoline costs $1.70 per liter. The car's tank holds 12 gallons. Use 1 gallon = 3.785 liters. How much will it cost to fill the empty tank? Enter the number of dollars, rounded to the nearest dollar.

tr.5: Divided 12 by 3.785 (3.17 L) instead of multiplying.
tr.20: Multiplied 12 by $1.70 without converting gallons to liters.

q: A newborn weighs 3,400 grams at birth, and the parents ask for the weight in pounds. Use 1 kilogram = 2.2 pounds. What is the newborn's weight in pounds? Enter the number of pounds, rounded to the nearest tenth.

tr.7480: Multiplied 3,400 g by 2.2 without first converting grams to kilograms.
tr.1.5: Divided 3.4 kg by 2.2; kilograms to pounds means multiplying.
tr.7.4: Truncated 7.48 instead of rounding; the hundredths digit 8 rounds the tenths digit up.

q: A pediatric clinic paints a height line on the wall at exactly 1 meter. Use 1 inch = 2.54 centimeters. Which of the following heights are greater than 1 meter? Select all that apply.
w: 1 m = 100 cm. 40 in × 2.54 = 101.6 cm; 1.1 yd = 39.6 in = 100.58 cm; 3 ft 3.5 in = 39.5 in = 100.33 cm. All three are over 100 cm. The others are 99.06 cm, 98.76 cm and 96.52 cm.

n.1: 39 × 2.54 = 99.06 cm, just under 100 cm.
n.4: 3 ft 2 in = 38 in, and 38 × 2.54 = 96.52 cm, under 100 cm.

q: A hospital cafeteria needs 12 gallons of soup for a staff event. The soup comes in 4-liter containers. Use 1 liter = 1.06 quarts. What is the least number of containers the cafeteria must order?
w: 12 gal × 4 = 48 qt. 48 ÷ 1.06 = 45.28 L. 45.28 ÷ 4 = 11.32, so round up to 12 containers.

n.1: This does not convert gallons to quarts (12 ÷ 1.06 = 11.3 L, then 11.3 ÷ 4 = 2.8); 1 gal = 4 qt.
n.2: 45.28 L ÷ 4 = 11.3, and 11 containers fall short, so round up.
n.3: This multiplies 48 qt by 1.06 (50.88) instead of dividing, then divides by 4 to get 12.7.

q: A wound measured 7.62 centimeters long at its first assessment. One week later, it was 2 inches shorter. Use 1 inch = 2.54 centimeters. What was the length of the wound, in centimeters, after one week?
w: 2 in × 2.54 = 5.08 cm. 7.62 - 5.08 = 2.54 cm (which is exactly 1 inch).

n.1: 1 is the new length in inches (3 in - 2 in); it was not converted back to centimeters.
n.2: This divides 2 by 2.54 (0.79) instead of multiplying, then subtracts.
n.3: This subtracts 2 directly from 7.62 without converting 2 inches to centimeters.

q: A hospital shuttle drives between a clinic and the main hospital, a distance of 18 kilometers one way. The shuttle makes 5 round trips each day. Use 1 mile = 1.6 kilometers. How many miles does the shuttle drive each day?
w: Round trip = 2 × 18 = 36 km; 5 round trips = 180 km. 180 ÷ 1.6 = 112.5 mi.

n.0: This counts 5 one-way trips; each round trip is 2 × 18 = 36 km.
n.2: This multiplies by 1.6 and also counts one-way trips (18 × 5 × 1.6).
n.3: This multiplies 180 km by 1.6; kilometers to miles means dividing by 1.6.

q: A newborn weighed 3.2 kilograms at birth and 3.65 kilograms at a two-week checkup. Use 1 ounce = 28 grams. To the nearest whole ounce, how much weight did the newborn gain?

n.0: This treats the 0.45 kg gain as 0.45 lb (7.2 oz) without converting kilograms.

q: A child weighs 44 pounds. The provider orders one dose of a medication at 10 milligrams per kilogram of body weight. The oral suspension contains 40 milligrams in every 5 milliliters. Use 1 kilogram = 2.2 pounds. How many milliliters make up one dose?

n.0: 200 ÷ 40 = 5 is the number of 5 mL portions in the dose; multiply by 5 mL to get 25 mL.

n.3: This multiplies 44 by 2.2 (96.8 kg) instead of dividing, which gives 968 mg and 121 mL.

q: A patient is prescribed 1 tablespoon of cough syrup three times a day for 5 days. The pharmacy needs the total volume in milliliters. How many milliliters of cough syrup will the patient take over the full 5 days?
w: 1 tbsp = 15 mL. Per day: 3 × 15 = 45 mL. For 5 days: 45 × 5 = 225 mL.

n.0: This uses 10 mL per tablespoon (2 teaspoons); 1 tbsp = 3 tsp = 15 mL.
n.2: This is one day's amount (3 × 15 mL); the course lasts 5 days.
n.3: This uses 5 mL, the volume of a teaspoon; 1 tbsp = 15 mL.

q: A child's liquid antibiotic dose is 1 1/2 teaspoons twice a day. The bottle holds 4 fluid ounces. Use 1 fluid ounce = 30 milliliters. How many full days will the bottle last at this dose?
w: Dose = 1.5 × 5 mL = 7.5 mL; per day = 2 × 7.5 = 15 mL. Bottle = 4 × 30 = 120 mL. 120 ÷ 15 = 8 days.

n.1: This counts one dose per day (120 ÷ 7.5); the dose is given twice a day.
n.2: This uses 15 mL per fluid ounce; the stem gives 1 fl oz = 30 mL.
n.3: This uses 15 mL per teaspoon, which is the tablespoon amount; 1 tsp = 5 mL.

q: A patient's oral temperature is recorded as 38.5 °C in the hospital chart. The patient's home thermometer reads in degrees Fahrenheit. What is the patient's temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?

n.1: This rounds 38.5 °C up to 39 °C before converting; round only at the end, and (9/5)(38.5) + 32 = 101.3 °F.
n.2: This adds the 1.5 °C above normal (37 °C) to 98.6 °F. Each Celsius degree equals 1.8 Fahrenheit degrees, so the reading is 2.7 °F above normal.
n.3: This multiplies by 2 instead of 9/5 (2 × 38.5 + 32 = 109); the factor is 9/5 = 1.8.

q: A vaccine refrigerator log lists a reading of 41 °F. The clinic's storage policy lists temperature limits in degrees Celsius. What is the refrigerator's temperature in degrees Celsius?

n.1: This subtracts 32 but then multiplies by 9/5 instead of 5/9.
n.2: This multiplies 41 by 5/9 without first subtracting 32.
n.3: This multiplies by 5/9 and then subtracts 32; subtract 32 first.

q: A child has a fever of 102.2 °F. The pediatric chart records temperatures in degrees Celsius. What is the child's temperature in degrees Celsius? Round to the nearest tenth if necessary, and enter the number only.

q: During one shift, a patient drinks 2 cups of broth, 6 fluid ounces of juice, and 3 tablespoons of a liquid supplement. Use 1 cup = 240 milliliters and 1 fluid ounce = 30 milliliters. What is the patient's total intake? Enter the number of milliliters.

w: Broth: 2 × 240 = 480 mL. Juice: 6 × 30 = 180 mL. Supplement: 3 × 15 = 45 mL. Total = 480 + 180 + 45 = 705 mL.

q: A research lab recorded five room temperatures, some in degrees Celsius and some in degrees Fahrenheit. Place the readings in order from coldest to warmest, starting with the coldest.
w: Convert the Celsius readings to °F with °F = (9/5)(°C) + 32: 14 °C = 57.2 °F; 15 °C = 59 °F; 16.5 °C = 61.7 °F. Coldest to warmest: 57.2 °F (14 °C), 58 °F, 59 °F (15 °C), 61 °F, 61.7 °F (16.5 °C).

q: A home oral rehydration recipe calls for 6 level teaspoons of sugar per liter of clean water. A parent is making 1.5 liters of the solution but has a tablespoon measure and no teaspoon. How many tablespoons of sugar are needed?
w: Teaspoons needed = 6 × 1.5 = 9 tsp. Since 1 tbsp = 3 tsp, 9 ÷ 3 = 3 tbsp.

n.0: 9 is the number of teaspoons (6 × 1.5); divide by 3 to change teaspoons to tablespoons.
n.1: This multiplies the 9 teaspoons by 3 instead of dividing.
n.3: This uses 2 teaspoons per tablespoon; 1 tbsp = 3 tsp.

q: A safety data sheet lists the storage temperature of a laboratory reagent as 298 kelvins. Use K = °C + 273. The lab's thermostat displays degrees Fahrenheit. What is the storage temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?

n.1: This changes to 25 °C correctly but then multiplies by 5/9 instead of 9/5 before adding 32.
n.2: This adds 32 to 25 °C without first multiplying by 9/5.
n.3: 25 is the temperature in degrees Celsius; it still has to be converted to °F.

q: A patient on a fluid restriction may drink no more than 1,800 milliliters per day. By early afternoon, the patient has had 3 cups of coffee and 10 fluid ounces of water. Use 1 cup = 240 milliliters and 1 fluid ounce = 30 milliliters. How many more milliliters may the patient drink today?
w: Coffee: 3 × 240 = 720 mL. Water: 10 × 30 = 300 mL. Total so far = 1,020 mL. Remaining = 1,800 - 1,020 = 780 mL.

n.0: 1,020 mL is the amount already taken; subtract it from 1,800 mL.
n.1: This counts 10 fl oz as 100 mL; 10 × 30 = 300 mL.
n.2: This subtracts the coffee (720 mL) but leaves out the 10 fl oz of water.

q: Between 8 a.m. and noon, a patient's temperature rose from 37.2 °C to 38.7 °C. The family asks how much the temperature went up in Fahrenheit terms. By how many degrees Fahrenheit did the temperature rise?

n.1: 1.5 is the rise in degrees Celsius; each Celsius degree equals 9/5 Fahrenheit degrees.
n.2: This adds 32 to the change. The 32 shifts the starting point of the scale, so it cancels out of a difference.
n.3: This multiplies the 1.5 °C change by 5/9 instead of 9/5.

q: A child takes 1/2 teaspoon of a liquid vitamin three times a day for 10 days. The oral syringe that comes with the bottle is marked in milliliters. How many milliliters of the vitamin will the child take over the 10 days?

n.0: This uses 15 mL per teaspoon, which is the tablespoon amount (7.5 mL per dose).
n.1: This is one day's amount (3 × 2.5 mL); the course lasts 10 days.
n.3: This uses a full teaspoon (5 mL) per dose instead of 1/2 teaspoon.

q: A rectangular patient room measures 14 feet by 11 feet. New vinyl flooring costs $4.25 per square foot, including installation. What is the total cost to cover the entire floor of the room?

n.1: This takes half of the area, as if the floor were a triangle.
n.2: This uses 14 + 11 = 25, half the perimeter, instead of the area.
n.3: This uses the perimeter (2 × 14 + 2 × 11 = 50 ft) instead of the area.

q: A triangular flower bed has sides of 13 meters, 14 meters, and 15 meters. The perpendicular height from the 14-meter side to the opposite corner is 12 meters. What is the area of the flower bed?
w: A = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 14 × 12 = 84 m². The 13 m and 15 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

n.0: 42 m is the perimeter (13 + 14 + 15), not the area.
n.2: This multiplies base by height but leaves out the 1/2.
n.3: This uses the 15 m slanted side as the height (1/2 × 14 × 15); the height must be perpendicular to the base.

q: A wooden deck is shaped like a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are 18 feet and 12 feet long, and the perpendicular distance between them is 8 feet. What is the area of the deck?

n.1: This multiplies the longer base by the height, as if the deck were a rectangle.
n.2: This adds the bases and multiplies by the height but leaves out the 1/2.
n.3: This multiplies the shorter base by the height, as if the deck were a rectangle.

q: An L-shaped room is formed from a 20-foot by 12-foot rectangle with a 6-foot by 5-foot closet cut out of one corner. The closet is not part of the room. What is the floor area of the L-shaped room?
w: Full rectangle = 20 × 12 = 240 ft². Closet = 6 × 5 = 30 ft². Room = 240 - 30 = 210 ft².

n.0: This adds the closet area (30 ft²) instead of subtracting it.
n.1: 64 ft is the perimeter of the L-shaped room, not its area.
n.2: This is the full rectangle; the 30 ft² closet must be subtracted.

q: A rectangular garden measures 18 feet by 12 feet. A gravel path 3 feet wide surrounds the garden on all four sides. What is the area of the gravel path, not including the garden? Enter the number of square feet.

tr.99: Added the 3-foot width to one side of each dimension (21 ft by 15 ft = 315 ft²) before subtracting.
tr.180: Multiplied the garden's perimeter (60 ft) by 3 ft, which leaves out the four corner squares.
tr.432: Gave the area of the whole outer rectangle without subtracting the garden.

w: The path adds 3 ft on each side, so the outer rectangle is 18 + 6 = 24 ft by 12 + 6 = 18 ft. Outer area = 24 × 18 = 432 ft². Garden = 18 × 12 = 216 ft². Path = 432 - 216 = 216 ft².

q: A bedroom floor measures 4 yards by 5 yards. Carpet costs $2.50 per square foot, including installation. What is the total cost to carpet the entire floor? Enter the number of dollars.

tr.50: Multiplied 20 yd² by $2.50 without converting to square feet.
tr.150: Used 3 ft² per square yard; 1 yd² = 3 × 3 = 9 ft².

w: Convert lengths first: 4 yd = 12 ft and 5 yd = 15 ft. Area = 12 × 15 = 180 ft². Cost = 180 × $2.50 = $450. (Or 20 yd² × 9 = 180 ft².)

q: A designer needs a flat panel with an area of exactly 48 square inches. Which of the following shapes have an area of exactly 48 square inches? Select all that apply.
o: A parallelogram with base 16 in, slanted side 5 in, and height 3 in
A square with a perimeter of 48 in
A triangle with base 12 in and height 8 in
A parallelogram with base 12 in, slanted side 4 in, and height 3 in
A triangle with base 6 in and height 8 in
w: Rectangle: 6 × 8 = 48 in². Triangle: 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48 in². Parallelogram: 16 × 3 = 48 in² (use the perpendicular height, not the 5 in slanted side). The square is 144 in², the smaller triangle 24 in², and the other parallelogram 36 in².

n.1: Each side is 48 ÷ 4 = 12 in, so the area is 12 × 12 = 144 in²; 48 is the perimeter.
n.3: Area = base × perpendicular height = 12 × 3 = 36 in²; 48 comes from using the slanted side as the height.
n.5: 1/2 × 6 × 8 = 24 in²; 48 comes from leaving out the 1/2.

q: A square bulletin board covers 196 square inches of wall space. A teacher wants to staple decorative trim around its entire edge. How many inches of trim are needed?
w: Side = square root of 196 = 14 in, because 14 × 14 = 196. Perimeter = 4 × 14 = 56 in.

n.1: This divides the area by 2 instead of finding the side length.
n.2: 14 in is the length of one side, not the distance around the board.
n.3: This divides the area by 4; find the side length first (the square root of 196 is 14 in).

q: A rectangular dog run has a perimeter of 68 feet. Its length is 22 feet. A pet owner wants to cover the ground with artificial turf. What is the area of the dog run?
w: The two lengths use 2 × 22 = 44 ft. 68 - 44 = 24 ft for the two widths, so width = 12 ft. Area = 22 × 12 = 264 ft².

n.0: This uses 68 ÷ 4 = 17 ft as the width, as if the run were a square.
n.1: This takes the width as 68 - 2(22) = 24 ft, but 24 ft is both widths together.
n.2: This takes the width as 68 - 22 = 46 ft; both lengths must be subtracted, then the rest split between two widths.

q: On a floor plan, 1 inch represents 4 feet. A rectangular room on the plan measures 3 inches by 2.5 inches. What is the actual area of the room?
w: Actual sides: 3 × 4 = 12 ft and 2.5 × 4 = 10 ft. Area = 12 × 10 = 120 ft². (Check: 7.5 in² × 16 = 120 ft².)

n.0: 7.5 is the area on the plan in square inches, not the actual area.
n.1: This multiplies the plan's area (7.5 in²) by 4; areas scale by 4 × 4 = 16.
n.2: 44 ft is the actual perimeter (2 × 12 + 2 × 10), not the area.

q: A sign is shaped like a parallelogram with a base of 2.5 meters and slanted sides of 1.3 meters. The perpendicular height between the two bases is 1.2 meters. What is the area of one face of the sign?
w: A = base × perpendicular height = 2.5 × 1.2 = 3 m².

n.0: This multiplies the base by the slanted side; the height must be perpendicular to the base.
n.2: 7.6 m is the perimeter, 2 × (2.5 + 1.3), not the area.
n.3: This takes half of base × height, which is the triangle formula.

q: The front wall of a shed is a rectangle 10 feet wide and 8 feet tall, topped by a triangle with a 10-foot base and a 4-foot height. The wall has one 3-foot by 2-foot window. How many square feet of the wall need siding, not counting the window?
w: Rectangle = 10 × 8 = 80 ft². Triangle = 1/2 × 10 × 4 = 20 ft². Total = 100 ft². Window = 3 × 2 = 6 ft². Siding = 100 - 6 = 94 ft².

n.0: This subtracts the window from the rectangle (80 - 6) but leaves out the triangle.
n.2: This finds the total wall area (80 + 20) but does not subtract the 6 ft² window.
n.3: This uses 10 × 4 = 40 ft² for the triangle, leaving out the 1/2.

q: A clinic waiting room has a circular rug with a diameter of 8 feet. The staff want to know how much floor space the rug covers. What is the area of the rug? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.0: 25.12 is the circumference (3.14 × 8), a length rather than an area.
n.2: This multiplies pi by the radius (3.14 × 4) instead of by the radius squared.
n.3: This uses the diameter (8 ft) as the radius; r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 ft.

q: A wheelchair wheel has a radius of 14 inches. How far does the wheelchair travel when the wheel makes one complete turn without slipping? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: One turn moves the chair one circumference. C = 2πr = 2 × 3.14 × 14 = 87.92 in.

n.0: This finds the area (πr²) instead of the circumference.
n.1: This multiplies pi by the radius; circumference is 2πr.
n.2: This multiplies 2π by the diameter (28 in); use C = 2πr or C = πd.

q: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 26 inches. How many complete revolutions does the wheel make while the bicycle travels 100 feet in a straight line? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: C = πd = 3.14 × 26 = 81.64 in. 100 ft = 100 × 12 = 1,200 in. 1,200 ÷ 81.64 = 14.7, so the wheel makes 14 complete revolutions.

n.0: This uses the radius (13 in) in C = πd, which halves the circumference.
n.1: This uses C = 2πd (163.28 in), which doubles the circumference.
n.3: 1,200 ÷ 81.64 = 14.7, and the 15th revolution is not complete, so the answer is 14.

q: A decorative window is shaped like a semicircle with a straight bottom edge 4 feet long. A builder needs trim for the entire edge of the window, including the curved part and the straight bottom. How many feet of trim are needed? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: Curved part = 1/2 × πd = 1/2 × 3.14 × 4 = 6.28 ft. Add the straight edge (the diameter): 6.28 + 4 = 10.28 ft.

n.0: This adds the 4-foot straight edge to a full circle's circumference instead of half of it.
n.1: This is the circumference of a full circle (3.14 × 4).
n.3: This is the curved part by itself; the 4-foot straight edge must be added.

q: A circular garden has a circumference of 62.8 feet. The gardener needs its area to buy the right amount of mulch. What is the area of the garden? Use 3.14 for pi. Enter the number of square feet.

tr.100: Stopped at r² = 100 without multiplying by pi.
tr.1256: Used the diameter (20 ft) as the radius.
tr.31.4: Multiplied pi by the radius (3.14 × 10) instead of by the radius squared.

q: A square patio tabletop is 30 inches on each side. A circular hole with a diameter of 10 inches is cut out of the center for an umbrella pole. What is the area of the tabletop that remains? Use 3.14 for pi. Enter the number of square inches.

tr.586: Used the diameter (10 in) as the radius of the hole (3.14 × 100 = 314).
tr.868.6: Subtracted the hole's circumference (31.4 in) instead of its area.
tr.78.5: Gave the area of the hole instead of the area that remains.

w: Square = 30 × 30 = 900 in². Hole: r = 5 in, so A = 3.14 × 5² = 78.5 in². Remaining = 900 - 78.5 = 821.5 in².

q: A circular pizza with a diameter of 14 inches is cut into 8 equal slices. What is the area of one slice, to the nearest tenth of a square inch? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.0: This is the area of the whole pizza; divide it by the 8 slices.
n.1: This uses the diameter (14 in) as the radius.
n.2: This divides the circumference (43.96 in) by 8; the area of a slice comes from πr².

q: A clinic stocks two sizes of circular wound dressings. The small dressing has a radius of 3 centimeters, and the large dressing has a radius of 6 centimeters. How many more square centimeters does the large dressing cover? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.1: This uses the diameters (6 cm and 12 cm) as the radii.
n.2: This assumes doubling the radius doubles the area; it multiplies the area by 4.
n.3: This is the difference in circumferences (37.68 - 18.84), not in areas.

q: A lawn sprinkler waters a circular region with an area of 113.04 square meters. A landscaper needs the width of the region measured straight across through its center. What is the diameter of the watered region? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.0: 6 m is the radius; the diameter is twice the radius.
n.2: This divides the area by 2π (6.28), as if A = 2πr.
n.3: 36 is r²; take its square root to find r, then double it.

q: A circular pool with a radius of 9 feet is surrounded by a concrete walkway 3 feet wide. A fence will be built along the outer edge of the walkway. How long will the fence be? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: Outer radius = 9 + 3 = 12 ft. C = 2πr = 2 × 3.14 × 12 = 75.36 ft.

n.0: This is the area inside the fence (3.14 × 12²), not its length.
n.2: This uses the pool's radius (9 ft); the fence is at the outer edge, 12 ft from the center.
n.3: This adds the 3-foot walkway to the diameter once (21 ft); it adds 3 ft on each side (24 ft).

q: The minute hand of a wall clock in a nurses' station is 15 centimeters long. How far does the tip of the minute hand travel in 20 minutes? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: In 20 minutes the hand turns 20/60 = 1/3 of a circle. C = 2 × 3.14 × 15 = 94.2 cm. 94.2 ÷ 3 = 31.4 cm.

n.1: This takes 2/3 of the circumference; 20 minutes is 1/3 of an hour.
n.2: This takes 1/3 of πr (3.14 × 15) instead of 1/3 of 2πr.
n.3: This is the distance for a full hour, one complete circle.

q: A round table has a diameter of 5 feet. Each person seated at the table needs 2 feet of space along the table's edge. What is the greatest number of people who can be seated at the table? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: C = πd = 3.14 × 5 = 15.7 ft. 15.7 ÷ 2 = 7.85, so 7 people can be seated.

n.0: 15.7 ÷ 2 = 7.85, and an eighth person would not have a full 2 feet, so round down.
n.1: This uses the table's area (19.625 ft²) instead of the distance around it.
n.2: This uses the radius in C = πd (7.85 ft), which halves the edge length.

q: A rectangular storage bin in a hospital supply room is 2.5 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 1.5 feet tall. How many cubic feet of supplies can the bin hold when it is filled to the top?

n.0: This adds the three dimensions; volume multiplies them.
n.2: 23.5 is the surface area of the bin in square feet, 2(5 + 3.75 + 3), not its volume.
n.3: This multiplies the length by the height (2.5 × 1.5) but leaves out the width.

q: A cylindrical water tank behind a rural clinic has a radius of 3 feet and a height of 5 feet. What is the volume of the tank? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.1: This uses the diameter (6 ft) as the radius.
n.2: This uses 2πrh, the area of the curved side, instead of πr²h.
n.3: This multiplies pi by the radius once (3.14 × 3 × 5) instead of by r².

q: A rectangular fish tank in a pediatric waiting room measures 50 centimeters long, 30 centimeters wide, and 40 centimeters high. How many liters of water does the tank hold when it is completely full?

n.0: This divides 60,000 cm³ by 100; 1 L = 1,000 cm³.
n.2: This divides 60,000 cm³ by 10,000 instead of 1,000.
n.3: 60,000 is the volume in cubic centimeters (milliliters), not liters.

q: A cube-shaped gift box has edges 4 inches long. A second cube-shaped box has edges twice as long as the edges of the first box. What is the volume of the second box?
w: Each edge of the second box is 2 × 4 = 8 in. V = 8³ = 8 × 8 × 8 = 512 in³, which is 8 times the first box's 64 in³.

n.1: This multiplies the volume by 4, which is the scale factor for area, not volume.
n.2: 384 is the surface area of the larger cube in square inches (6 × 8²), not its volume.
n.3: This doubles the first box's volume (2 × 64); doubling every edge multiplies volume by 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

q: A cylindrical can has a diameter of 8 centimeters and a height of 12 centimeters. How many milliliters can the can hold? Use 3.14 for pi and 1 cubic centimeter = 1 milliliter. Enter the number of milliliters, rounded to the nearest whole number.

tr.301: Multiplied pi by the diameter and the height (3.14 × 8 × 12) without squaring the radius.
tr.2412: Used the diameter (8 cm) as the radius: 3.14 × 64 × 12 = 2,411.52.

w: r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. V = πr²h = 3.14 × 16 × 12 = 602.88 cm³ = 602.88 mL, which rounds to 603 mL.

q: A closed rectangular box measures 10 inches long, 6 inches wide, and 4 inches high. How many square inches of wrapping paper are needed to cover the entire outside of the box with no overlap? Enter the number of square inches.

tr.124: Added the three different faces once; each face has a matching opposite face.
tr.240: Found the volume (10 × 6 × 4) instead of the surface area.

q: Five containers are being compared for a supply room. Use 3.14 for pi and 1 milliliter = 1 cubic centimeter. Place the containers in order from least volume to greatest volume, starting with the least.
o: A box 8 cm by 12 cm by 11 cm
A cylinder with radius 5 cm and height 12 cm
w: Convert each to cubic centimeters: cylinder = 3.14 × 5² × 12 = 942; bottle = 0.95 L = 950 mL = 950; cube = 10³ = 1,000; jug = 1,020; box = 8 × 12 × 11 = 1,056. Least to greatest: 942, 950, 1,000, 1,020, 1,056.

q: A cone-shaped paper water cup has a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters. What is the volume of the cup when it is filled to the brim? Use 3.14 for pi.

n.0: This uses r instead of r²: 1/3 × 3.14 × 3 × 10.
n.1: This uses the cylinder formula πr²h; a cone holds 1/3 of that.
n.3: This uses the diameter (6 cm) as the radius.

q: A rectangular wading pool is 20 feet long and 10 feet wide and will be filled to a depth of 4 feet. Use 1 cubic foot = 7.5 gallons. A hose fills the pool at 50 gallons per minute. How many hours will it take to fill the pool?

n.1: This divides the 800 cubic feet by the rate (16 minutes) without converting to gallons.
n.2: This reads 120 minutes as 1.2 hours; 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.
n.3: 120 is the time in minutes; it must be divided by 60 to give hours.

q: A rectangular planter box holds 9 cubic feet of soil when filled to the top. The base of the box is 4 feet long and 1.5 feet wide. How deep is the planter box, in inches?

n.1: 1.5 is the depth in feet; 1.5 ft × 12 = 18 in.
n.2: This divides by the length (9 ÷ 4 = 2.25 ft) but leaves out the width.
n.3: This treats 1.5 ft as 15 in, as if a foot had 10 inches; 1.5 ft = 18 in.

q: A closed cylindrical can has a radius of 3 inches and a height of 8 inches. A paper label covers the curved side of the can but not the top or bottom. What is the area of the label? Use 3.14 for pi.
w: Unrolled, the label is a rectangle: circumference × height. Area = 2πrh = 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 8 = 150.72 in².

n.0: This uses πrh; the curved side's area is 2πrh (circumference × height).
n.1: 226.08 is the volume (πr²h) in cubic inches, not the label's area.
n.2: This adds the top and bottom circles (2 × 28.26 in²); the label covers the curved side.

q: A storage room is 4 yards long, 3 yards wide, and 3 yards high. A ventilation fan is sized by the number of cubic feet of air in the room. What is the volume of the room in cubic feet?
w: V = 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 yd³. 36 × 27 = 972 ft³. (Or convert first: 12 ft × 9 ft × 9 ft = 972 ft³.)

n.0: 36 is the volume in cubic yards, not cubic feet.
n.1: This multiplies 36 yd³ by 3; 1 yd³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 ft³.
n.2: This multiplies 36 yd³ by 9, which is the square-yard factor.

q: A 13-foot ladder leans against the wall of a building. The foot of the ladder rests on level ground 5 feet from the base of the wall. How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
w: The ladder is the hypotenuse. h² = 13² - 5² = 169 - 25 = 144, so h = 12 ft (a 5-12-13 right triangle).

n.0: This subtracts 5 instead of 5² (169 - 5 = 164, and the square root of 164 is about 12.8).
n.1: This doubles each length instead of squaring it (26 - 10 = 16, and the square root of 16 is 4).
n.2: This subtracts the lengths (13 - 5); the Pythagorean theorem works with the squares of the sides.

q: A rectangular television screen is 48 inches wide and 20 inches tall. Screen size is measured along the diagonal from one corner to the opposite corner. What is the diagonal length of the screen?

n.0: This subtracts the squares (2,304 - 400); the diagonal is the hypotenuse, so add them.
n.1: This adds the sides (48 + 20); the diagonal is found with a² + b² = c².
n.3: This doubles 20 instead of squaring it (2,304 + 40 = 2,344, and the square root of 2,344 is about 48.4).

q: In triangle PQR, angle P measures 38°, and angle Q measures twice as much as angle P. A student needs the third angle to finish a drawing. What is the measure of angle R?

n.1: This finds the complement of angle P (90 - 38); the angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
n.2: This subtracts angle P (180 - 38) but not angle Q.
n.3: This subtracts angle Q (180 - 76) but not angle P; both must be subtracted.

q: Two straight roads cross each other, forming four angles at the intersection. One of the angles measures 57°. What are the measures of the angle vertical (directly opposite) to it and of an angle adjacent to it?
w: Vertical angles are equal, so the opposite angle is 57°. An adjacent angle forms a straight line with the 57° angle, so it is 180 - 57 = 123°.

n.0: This reverses the rules. Vertical angles are equal (57°); adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary (123°).
n.1: This uses 90° for the adjacent angle; angles along a straight line sum to 180°.
n.3: This takes the complement for the vertical angle; vertical angles are equal.

q: A rectangular park is 240 meters long and 100 meters wide. Instead of walking along two sides of the park to reach the opposite corner, a jogger takes a straight diagonal path. How many meters shorter is the diagonal route? Enter the number of meters.

tr.200: Used 240 - 100 = 140 m as the diagonal instead of the Pythagorean theorem.
tr.260: Gave the length of the diagonal instead of the distance saved.
tr.340: Gave the distance along the two sides instead of the distance saved.

q: The roof truss of a house is an isosceles triangle. The angle at the peak, between the two equal sloping sides, measures 112°. What is the measure of each of the two base angles of the truss?
w: In an isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal. (180 - 112) ÷ 2 = 68 ÷ 2 = 34°.

n.0: This uses 360°, the angle sum of a quadrilateral, instead of 180°.
n.1: 68° is both base angles together (180 - 112); divide by 2.
n.3: This halves the peak angle; the base angles share what is left of 180°.

q: A gazebo floor is shaped like a regular hexagon. A carpenter needs the angle at each corner to cut the floorboards. What is the measure of each interior angle of the floor?
w: Sum of interior angles = (n - 2) × 180 = (6 - 2) × 180 = 720°. Each angle = 720 ÷ 6 = 120°.

n.1: 108° is each interior angle of a regular pentagon (5 sides).
n.2: 720° is the sum of all six interior angles; divide by 6.
n.3: 60° is each exterior angle (360 ÷ 6); an interior angle and its exterior angle sum to 180°.

q: At the same time of day, a 6-foot-tall nurse casts a shadow 4 feet long, and a flagpole outside the clinic casts a shadow 22 feet long. The two right triangles formed are similar. How tall is the flagpole?
w: Height to shadow is the same in both triangles: 6/4 = h/22. h = 22 × 6 ÷ 4 = 33 ft.

n.1: This sets up the ratio upside down (22 × 4 ÷ 6).
n.2: This adds the 2-foot difference between height and shadow; similar triangles scale by multiplying.
n.3: This multiplies 6 by 22 but does not divide by the 4-foot shadow.

q: Two angles in a shelf bracket design are complementary. The larger angle measures 12° more than twice the smaller angle. What is the measure of the larger angle?
w: Let the smaller angle be x. x + (2x + 12) = 90, so 3x = 78 and x = 26. Larger = 2(26) + 12 = 64°. Check: 26 + 64 = 90.

n.0: This uses 180° (supplementary): 3x + 12 = 180 gives x = 56 and a larger angle of 124°.
n.1: This leaves out the 12°: 3x = 90 gives x = 30 and a larger angle of 60°.
n.3: 26° is the smaller angle; the larger is 2(26) + 12 = 64°.

q: A student is sorting triangles by type for a geometry project. Which set of side lengths forms a right triangle?
w: Test a² + b² = c² with the longest side as c: 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². Only this set satisfies the Pythagorean theorem.

n.0: 8² + 15² = 289, which is 17², not 18² = 324.
n.3: 5² + 12² = 169, which is 13², not 14² = 196.

q: A triangle has two angles that measure 35° and 55°. Which statements about the triangle must be true? Select all that apply.
o: The longest side is opposite the third angle.
w: Third angle = 180 - 35 - 55 = 90°, so it is a right triangle. 35 + 55 = 90, so those two angles are complementary. The longest side (the hypotenuse) is opposite the largest angle, the 90° angle.

n.1: 35° + 55° = 90°, so the angles are complementary; supplementary angles sum to 180°.
n.3: The third angle is 90°, so it is a right triangle; an acute triangle has all three angles under 90°.
n.4: The angles 35°, 55° and 90° are all different, so no two sides are equal; the triangle is scalene.

q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 17 centimeters and one leg of 8 centimeters. A designer needs the triangle's area to plan a tile pattern. What is the area of the triangle?
w: Other leg: 17² - 8² = 289 - 64 = 225, so the leg is 15 cm. A = 1/2 × 8 × 15 = 60 cm².

n.0: This multiplies the given leg by the hypotenuse (8 × 17) with no 1/2.
n.2: This multiplies the legs (8 × 15) but leaves out the 1/2.
n.3: This uses the hypotenuse as the height (1/2 × 8 × 17); the two legs are the base and height.

q: A pharmacy student converted six metric measurements. Select the conversion that is incorrect.
w: 1 g = 1,000 mg, so 0.6 g = 0.6 x 1,000 = 600 mg. The listed 60 mg uses a factor of 100 instead of 1,000.

q: A dietary aide converted six US customary measurements. Select the conversion that is incorrect.
w: 1 qt = 2 pt and 1 pt = 2 cups, so 1 qt = 4 cups and 3 qt = 3 x 4 = 12 cups. The listed 6 cups uses 1 qt = 2 cups.

n.d: 1 gal = 4 qt = 8 pt, so 1.5 x 8 = 12 pt.
n.f: 1 cup = 8 fl oz, so 48 / 8 = 6 cups. The same answer as the 3 qt row is correct here.

q: A nursing student converted six values using 1 in = 2.54 cm, 1 kg = 2.2 lb, 1 tsp = 5 mL, 1 fl oz = 30 mL, and °F = 1.8 x °C + 32. Select the conversion that is incorrect.
w: °F = 1.8 x 35 + 32 = 63 + 32 = 95 °F. The listed 63 °F multiplies by 1.8 but leaves out the + 32.

n.b: Kilograms to pounds: multiply. 55 x 2.2 = 121 lb.
